title: Rotated startup logs escape retention cleanup
test: tests/startupLogRetention.test.js: 'pruning removes the .log, .log.1 and .log.2 of every session beyond the newest ten', 'the newest ten sessions keep every generation', 'a pruned session whose primary file is already gone loses its leftover generations', 'sessions that rotated a different number of times are grouped by their stem', 'startup-latest.log, its generations and unrelated files are never pruned', 'ten sessions or fewer, including rotated ones, are all kept', 'the keep option sets how many sessions stay', 'the session pattern captures the stem and an optional numeric generation', 'an empty or missing log directory is a no-op', 'pruning failures are swallowed and the other files are still removed', 'lib/startupRuntime.js prunes with the helper when it starts' (a child process with NEXTRA_LOG_DIR pointing at a temporary directory), 'the helper ships with the packaged app: it sits in lib/, which the packager copies whole, and needs only Node'
proof: Run against the unchanged pruning logic (moved verbatim into lib/startupLogRetention.js so a test can load it; lib/startupRuntime.js cannot be required because it patches process.stdout/stderr on load): with 13 sessions of .log, .log.1 and .log.2 in a temporary directory, the 3 oldest sessions lost only their .log and kept .log.1 and .log.2 ('startup-20200101-120000-4001.log.1 should have been pruned with its session'); a session whose .log was already gone was never touched; and the real lib/startupRuntime.js run in a child process with 12 such sessions left the oldest two sessions' rotated files behind (same message). 5 of the 13 tests failed for that reason (4 more failed only because the verbatim extraction takes no keep option and returns no list of removed names). After the fix lib/startupLogRetention.js groups files by the stem captured by /^(startup-\d{8}-\d{6}-\d+)\.log(?:\.\d+)?$/, sorts the stems descending as before, keeps 10 and deletes every file of the others; all 13 tests pass. startup-latest.log* and any name that is not a session log (.bak, .log.1.old, a malformed stem) are untouched; every unlink and the directory read stay in try/catch. The packaged build needs no package-app.js change: scripts/package-app.js copies 'lib' as a directory (sourceEntries), and a test pins that. Output of the failing run: .arbitra/dev-notes/results/TASK-031-before.txt. The real packager was not run (not asked for and forbidden here).
